scale_note: Scale 1:25,000 on the sheet; the scan is a reduced photocopy, about 2.6 m per pixel.
note: A blue-line photocopy drawn with north to the left; shown turned to north-up. Fitted to the ground on nine places that still stand (churches, the Walled City's south bastion, Paco cemetery, Malacanang): places on it fall within about 170 m of where they are, at worst 270 m. "Former ... outpost" labels are positions before the battle; the heavy double-dashed lines named for regiments are their final positions, after the capture of Caloocan on 10 Feb. South of the city this sketch is not to scale: placed on the ground with the rest of the sheet, its Pasay falls 1.3 km south-east of Pasay. Since 21 Nov 2026 the units are placed on the ground itself, so from Malate to Pasay and San Pedro Macati they stand up to 1.2 km north-west of the lines this map draws for them. The reconstructed map shows them on the right ground.

note: Drawn to go with General Young's report, with the roads his troops used and the dates of their fights. Much of the interior had never been surveyed and the map shows it: fitted to today's ground on 18 towns, places on it are typically 2 km from where they are, and up to 5 km in the mountains and at Vigan. Units are drawn where the towns really are, so they can sit a little off the map's own town marks.

note: The War Department's printed map of the theatre, compiled in Washington in 1899 from older Spanish mapping, on two sheets: Lingayen Gulf to Malolos, and Manila Bay to Lake Taal. It is the clearest of the three period maps and not the truest: fitted on 32 towns, places on the north sheet fall about 1.7 km from where they are (3.5 km at worst), and the Pacific coast is some 5 km out; the south sheet is within about half a kilometre at Manila and 1.4 km around Laguna de Bay (3.8 km at worst), and Cavite is 3 to 5 km out. The two sheets are fitted together so that they meet. Units are drawn at the true places. Zoomed in, the north sheet sharpens; the south sheet does not.
